title: How long houseplants can wait between waterings in summer
text:
These are summer averages for a plant in a 15 cm plastic pot in a bright room, counted from a full watering until the soil is dry at the bottom of the pot.
A peace lily can wait only about 5 days, and its leaves droop as soon as it is thirsty.
Pothos can wait about 10 days, and its leaves curl slightly when the soil is dry.
Aloe vera can wait about 14 days, because its thick leaves hold water.
A small cactus can wait about 18 days in summer, when it is growing, and much longer in winter.
A snake plant can wait about 25 days between waterings.
The ZZ plant can wait about 30 days, the longest on this list, because it stores water in thick rhizomes under the soil.
A clay pot, a hot balcony or a smaller pot will dry out sooner than these averages.
